answer: To resist sybils, each agent must continuously publish a work signal: a hash-chained log of peer-attested jobs paid for with non-transferable compute or sensor capacity. Clone farms can wander across many cheap addresses, yet they cannot keep every log current, because each attestation burns scarce capacity that cannot be copied. When duplicates collide, peers emit a shared plume of conflicting attestations that slashes the cluster's bond and bars it from future markets, so identities are cheap to spawn but expensive to keep live.
